highlights:
## A clearer clue when an app says no

Open **Apps** and try starting the connection again. If it stops before sign-in, Nod now shows the connection service's HTTP status and a recognized reason instead of a generic failure. Share what you see in feedback, and we can tell a rate limit from a temporary service problem without guessing.

If an Attio request gets a Cloudflare HTML 403, Nod adds the UTC time and a validated Ray ID when one is available. Send those details in feedback too. They help trace the request; they do not change the access rule.

## Background checks take a breath

After a known connection-service 429 or 503, Gmail waits for its next scheduled inbox check instead of retrying immediately. Your inbox cursor and completed messages stay in place for that later check. Disabled or replaced scheduled jobs also stop asking for connection watch status, so stale work makes fewer background calls.
